title: 3DBAG Semantic Attribute Specification Schema
description: Schema for resources/semantic/attributes.json, the format-independent semantic model of 3DBAG attributes. Format-specific locations, physical types, and serialization live in resources/projections/, not here. Pinned review decisions: valueFormat is optional and descriptive for non-temporal values; date and datetime require a non-empty Chrono/strftime format checked by bundle validation; precision is max decimal places (0-17), rounded half-to-even in float64 before narrowing to a physical type, and must be absent for non-float types (enforced by the validator, not expressible in draft-07); array items reuse the value definition (attribute = value + source + items), the item-only "null" type is dropped in favor of item-level nullable; required fields are type, description, semanticType, source, nullable; empty attribute names are rejected via propertyNames.

semanticType.description: What is the attribute? A year, a day, a millisecond, an error etc.

nullable.description: Whether null values are valid for this attribute or they indicate an error in the process.

precision.description: Maximum number of digits after the decimal point (decimal places, not significant digits). Round half-to-even in float64 first, then narrow to the physical type declared by the projection. Only valid for type float; must be absent otherwise.

scale.description: How is the attribute measured? On an interval scale, on a nominal scale etc.

valueFormat.description: Optional pattern describing the logical value. Date and datetime require a non-empty Chrono/strftime pattern (e.g. '%Y-%m-%d') that consumers use for parsing and serialization. Other types may use a free-form description (e.g. 'NL.IMBAG.Pand.<16 digits>' or 'YYYY' for a year stored as int); it is not a parsing rule.

items.description: Recursive definition for each item of an array value.

type.description: How is the attribute stored? As an int, as a float etc. 'array' requires 'items'.

semanticType.description: What is the attribute? A year, a day, a millisecond, an error etc.

source.description: The source of this attribute. It can be another data set like the BAG or a software that generates this attribute.

nullable.description: Whether null values are valid for this attribute or they indicate an error in the process.

precision.description: Maximum number of digits after the decimal point (decimal places, not significant digits). Round half-to-even in float64 first, then narrow to the physical type declared by the projection. Only valid for type float; must be absent otherwise.

scale.description: How is the attribute measured? On an interval scale, on a nominal scale etc.

valueFormat.description: Optional pattern describing the logical value. Date and datetime require a non-empty Chrono/strftime pattern (e.g. '%Y-%m-%d') that consumers use for parsing and serialization. Other types may use a free-form description (e.g. 'NL.IMBAG.Pand.<16 digits>' or 'YYYY' for a year stored as int); it is not a parsing rule. Originallybouwjaar is intentionally int + 'YYYY' because source data contains invalid years (e.g. 9999) that must be preserved, not parsed as dates.

items.description: Recursive definition for each item of an array-type attribute.

value-type.description: Logical value type of a semantic value; arrays may recursively contain other values.
